- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market pessimism reversal.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was bullish; cap forecast at 1-2% below peak.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment oscillating), model often fails to correct quickly; apply smoothing or lagged mean adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, model underperforms when sentiment is mixed or volatile; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 7-14 day mean.
- If sentiment history shows strong negative sentiment followed by a rebound, model often misses the rebound; forecast should be 1-3% higher than prior low.
